summary: Scan of the signed WA/2011/192 six-month accelerated stability report for Esmervane Pharmaceuticals (EP19 capsule blend, lot L02), May 2012. Assay and impurities stayed within the protocol specification at all conditions; the specified degradant Imp A (RRT 0.86) increased at 40 °C/75% RH while water content showed no matching trend. Hydrolysis is proposed as a hypothesis to confirm. Faint approval stamp and a handwritten margin note on the moisture barrier.

document.header: WA/2011/192 | EP19 Lot L02 | 6-month report | Rev 00

title_block.title: STABILITY REPORT: EP19 CAPSULE BLEND, LOT L02
title_block.subtitle: Six-month accelerated data

blocks.p: 1.1 This report gives results for lot L02 of the EP19 capsule blend stored under protocol WA/2011/192 for up to six months. Storage started on 07/11/2011. 1.2 Conclusions are limited to the tested interval and conditions.

list: 2.1 Stability lot: EP19 capsule blend, lot L02, filled into size 1 hard gelatin capsules
2.2 Pack: 60 cc HDPE bottle, induction-sealed, 1 g silica gel desiccant, 30 capsules per bottle
2.3 Storage: 25 °C/60% RH, 30 °C/65% RH and 40 °C/75% RH in mapped chambers
3.1 Assay and related substances: HPLC method WA-AM-0412 Rev 02 (qualified 10/2011), UV 254 nm
3.3 System suitability per sequence: resolution Imp A / main peak ≥2.0, tailing ≤1.5, %RSD of six standard injections ≤1.0%

blocks.p: 3.4 All sequences in this report met system suitability.
4.1 Assay 95.0-105.0% of label claim; Imp A (RRT 0.86, specified) ≤0.50%; Imp B (RRT 1.12, specified) ≤0.30%; any unspecified impurity ≤0.20%; total impurities ≤2.0%.
5.1 Initial assay {{PRJ0086:stability.t0_assay}}% of label claim. Results to {{PRJ0086:stability.last_timepoint_months}} months are tabulated below.

6.1 All results comply with the specification. Assay and impurities are essentially unchanged at 25 °C/60% RH and 30 °C/65% RH. 6.2 At 40 °C/75% RH, Imp A increases with time. Water content does not show a matching upward trend, so moisture uptake through the pack is not demonstrated; hydrolysis of the amide is a hypothesis that should be confirmed by identifying the degradant and by a humidity-controlled comparison. 6.3 A tighter moisture barrier should be evaluated before long-term testing.
8.1 Sequence sheets, chromatograms and chamber records are held under WST-11-005959.
